stem: In the context of normal sleep physiology, during which part of the night does slow-wave sleep (Stages 3 and 4) primarily occur?

options.text: The first third of the night
The middle third of the night
The last third of the night

explanation: Slow-wave sleep, which includes non-REM stages 3 and 4, is most concentrated during the initial third of the sleep period.
rationale: Consider which stage of sleep is associated with the first few hours after falling asleep.

optionExplanations.A: Slow-wave sleep, which includes non-REM stages 3 and 4, is most concentrated during the initial third of the sleep period.
optionExplanations.B: While slow-wave sleep may occur here, it is physiologically dominant earlier in the sleep cycle.
optionExplanations.C: The final portion of the night is typically dominated by REM sleep, or 'dream sleep,' rather than slow-wave sleep.
optionExplanations.D: Sleep stages are not distributed evenly; different stages predominate at different times according to sleep architecture.

source.hint: Consider which stage of sleep is associated with the first few hours after falling asleep.
